reviews.title: LƯU THẾ BẢO · IELTS 49 · W07 · Đề 1
reviews.overall: Em đã viết đúng đề, dùng đúng số xe và chia hai đoạn Detail theo mốc 2006. Tuy nhiên, bài mới có 139 từ, chưa đạt mức tối thiểu 150 từ. Overview chưa nói Australia giảm liên tục, trong khi đây là xu hướng đối lập quan trọng. Ở Detail, “gradual rise” chưa phù hợp với các mức tăng lớn và hai mốc số liệu không cho thấy quá trình tăng dần; “kept declining” cũng khiến người đọc hiểu sai diễn biến của Thailand. Cô yêu cầu em bổ sung so sánh có ích, sửa các cụm này và đếm lại số từ trước khi nộp.
reviews.dataGrouping: Em chia theo 2003–2006 và 2006–2009, đúng với mốc Thailand đạt đỉnh và Argentina vượt Australia vào năm 2006. Mỗi Detail có hai câu, có đủ các mốc chính và dùng “conversely” để đối chiếu Australia với hai nước tăng trong giai đoạn đầu. Em nên nói rõ lần vượt của Argentina và giữ riêng chiều biến động của Thailand, Australia trong giai đoạn sau.

reviews.originalEssay:
The table illustrates the number of cars produced in three countries in 2003, 2006, and 2009.

Overall, there was a general increase in the number of cars made in Argentina and Thailand, with Argentina witnessing the most pronounced rise. Also of note is that Thailand consistently had the highest figure throughout the period, despite a decrease in the final year.

To elaborate, in 2003, 235,088 and 735,852 cars were produced in Argentina and Thailand, with a subsequent gradual rise to 352,759 and 1,162,356 respectively in 2006. The figure for Australia, conversely, fell from 452,163 to 341,268 over the same period.

Regarding the latter half of the provided timeline, the number of cars made in Argentina continued to go up, reaching 466,089 in 2009. Finally, the production of Thailand and Australia kept declining to 999,963 and 245,624 respectively in 2009.

Overall, car production rose steadily in Argentina and fell steadily in Australia. Thailand recorded the highest figure in all three years, climbing to a peak in 2006 before declining in 2009; nevertheless, its final figure remained above the 2003 level.

In 2003, Argentina produced 235,088 cars, compared with 452,163 in Australia and 735,852 in Thailand. By 2006, the figures for Argentina and Thailand had increased to 352,759 and 1,162,356 respectively, while Australia's had dropped to 341,268. From 2006 to 2009, the number of cars made in Argentina rose further to 466,089, making it the only country with uninterrupted growth. In contrast, Thailand's output fell from its 2006 peak to 999,963 cars, although it remained the largest producer. Australia's figure declined further to 245,624, leaving it well below Argentina by the end of the period.

reviews.overall: Em viết đúng đề và đủ 153 từ, có bốn đoạn và so sánh được số tù nhân nam luôn cao hơn số tù nhân nữ. Tuy nhiên, em viết số nam tăng dần từ 1911 đến 1971, trong khi biểu đồ cho thấy số này giảm mạnh vào năm 1931 rồi mới phục hồi. Phần nữ chỉ nêu hai đầu mốc, bỏ qua mức thấp nhất năm 1941 và lần tăng rồi giảm ở giữa kỳ. Cô yêu cầu em đọc lại các điểm đổi chiều và viết lại Overview cùng hai đoạn Detail để người đọc thấy đúng diễn biến.

Cách chia theo thời gian có thể dùng, nhưng đoạn đầu đã nối hai đầu mốc thành xu hướng tăng hoặc giảm đều và che mất các lần đổi chiều. Ở biểu đồ này, em có thể dành một Detail cho nam và một Detail cho nữ để trình bày rõ đáy, sự phục hồi và điểm cuối của từng đường.

Overall, there was a general increase in the male prison population, while an overall decrease was observed in the female prison population. Also of note is that the male prison population consistently had the highest figure throughout the period.
To elaborate, in 1911, there were around 18,000 male prisoners, with a subsequent gradual rise to 20,000 in 1971. The figure for female prisoners, conversely, fell from 3,200 to 700 over the same period of time.
Regarding the latter half of the provided timeline, the male prison population continued to go up, but to a far greater extent, reaching around 47,000 in 2001, marking the highest point of the entire chart. Likewise, a growth was recorded in the figure for female prisoners, yet it was less noticeable, increasing to around 2,000 in 2001.

The two line graphs show how the numbers of male and female prisoners in a European country changed between 1911 and 2001.

Overall, male prisoners outnumbered female prisoners throughout the period. The male total fell early on before recovering and then rising sharply after 1971, whereas the female total dropped substantially to a low in 1941 and subsequently fluctuated. In 1911, there were about 18,000 male prisoners, and this figure was almost unchanged in 1921. It then fell to approximately 10,000 in 1931, its lowest point, before recovering to nearly 20,000 by 1951. The number remained close to this level until 1971, after which it almost doubled to around 39,000 in 1981 and reached roughly 46,000 in 2001, the highest male figure shown.

By contrast, the female prison population began at roughly 3,200 in 1911. It declined steadily to about 500 in 1941, then rose to around 1,500 by 1961. After dropping back to approximately 700 in 1971, it increased to about 1,900 by 2001. Even at the start, the female count was far below the male count.

The line chart compares weekly per-person consumption of chicken, beef, lamb and fish in a European country between 1979 and 2004, measured in grams.

Overall, chicken consumption rose markedly and overtook beef around the late 1980s to finish as the most consumed category. Beef and lamb declined substantially, whereas fish fell only slightly and remained the least consumed throughout.

In 1979, beef consumption stood at roughly 220 grams per person per week, compared with about 140 grams for chicken. Beef climbed to a peak of approximately 240 grams in the early 1980s, then fluctuated downward to around 110 grams by 2004. Chicken, by contrast, rose with minor fluctuations, passing beef around 1988–1989 before reaching just over 250 grams at the end.

Regarding lamb and fish, lamb consumption began at about 150 grams per person per week and generally declined to roughly 55 grams in 2004, despite small rebounds. The figure for fish started at approximately 60 grams, stayed mostly around 40–50 grams during the intervening years, and ended at about 35 grams. Thus, the decline in fish consumption was far gentler than that for lamb.

reviews.originalEssay:
The given pie charts compare the primary reasons why UK students selected a specific university in two different years: 1997 and 2007.
           Overall, suitable degree courses remained the most popular reason for choosing a university throughout the period. Also of note is that while the proportion of students choosing an institution due to proximity to parental home and quality of teaching increased, the opposite was true for the remaining factors.
           To elaborate, starting at the leading position of 35% in 1997, the percentage of students choosing a school based on suitable degree courses went up slightly to 37% after 10 years, which remained the highest figure on the chart. Likewise, proximity to parental home witnessed a dramatic rise, more than doubling from 10% to 22% over the same period to become the second most influential factor. Meanwhile, quality of teaching also saw a modest increase from 15% in 1997 to 18% in 2007.
            In contrast, the figure for quality of resources experienced a moderate decline, dropping from 21% down to 17% between 1997 and 2007. Finally, good sports and social activities witnessed the most significant reduction, falling sharply from 19% to merely 6% in 2007, making it the least important reason by the end of the timeframe.
